subject: Upgrade pathway and commit adjustment / credit swap
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@apexanalytics.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Apex Analytics Procurement <procurement@apexanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Looking to accelerate capacity — renewal window callout

Hi Priyom,

Hope you’re well. We’re kicking off budget planning and would like to accelerate our Redwood capacity by ~40% starting May 1 to support a new pilot. Our current renewal is June 30. Before we sign a full-year commit increase, procurement asked whether Redwood can: 1) hold today’s list price for 12 months for the current unit price on the increased tier, or 2) offer bridge credits if we lock a partial commit now and full commit at renewal.

I attached a short usage export for Q1 (Apex_usage_Q1_2027.csv). Could we set a quick call to discuss options and get a draft amendment?

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Cloud AI Platforms
Apex Analytics

Attachment: Apex_usage_Q1_2027.csv (CSV, 48KB)

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@apexanalytics.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Looking to accelerate capacity — renewal window callout

Hi Elena — thanks for the context and the export. Happy to help. High level options we can bring to procurement on a short timeline:

- Price hold: we can offer to hold the current unit price on the expanded capacity for 9–12 months if Apex signs an upsell amendment now with a 9-month minimum commit.
- Bridge credits: if you prefer not to increase committed spend today, we can provide a pool of non-refundable credits that cover expected overage until the renewal; credits step down as you move into a full commit at renewal.
- Phased commit: a staged commit that scales May -> Aug -> Renewal month with defined floors and breakpoints.

I’ve looped in Monica (who owns renewals) and Rishi (discount approvals) to propose a specific amendment and credit schedule. Available for a 30-min call tomorrow at 10am PT if that works.

— Priyom
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_amendment_v1.pdf (placeholder — will share draft after internal alignment)

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-22T13:46:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Looking to accelerate capacity — renewal window callout

Folks — forwarding Elena’s ask. My read: priority is predictable unit economics for the pilot so they can launch without last-minute budget escalations. Two internal constraints to keep in mind: 1) discount tiers require VP sign-off for >20% effective discount; 2) credits for one-off overage should be non-refundable and bucketized to avoid indefinite liability.

Suggested approach before we talk to Apex:
- Offer a 9-month price hold at current unit rate on an incremental +40% capacity with a commitment floor at 70% utilization of the new tier.
- Provide $75k in bridge credits expiring at renewal; credits apply to overage only.
- Include a 30% partial refund clause if they convert to an annual commit above 150% of current usage within 60 days after renewal. (This gives them upside while capping our risk.)

Rishi — can you pre-clear the effective discount math and authority path? I’ll draft amendment language and a short procurement memo.

— Monica
Renewals Lead, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-22T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Looking to accelerate capacity — renewal window callout

Quick check — ran scenarios against their Q1 export. If we do the 9-month price hold on +40% incremental with the $75k bridge credit, the effective blended discount is ~18.5% on incremental units (volume-weighted). That stays under the 20% VP threshold, so SOC sign-off not required; I’ll still log the approval.

One ask: we should define a clear reversion point if utilization stays below 55% for three consecutive months — revert to pay-as-you-go for incremental capacity. That prevents a long tail.

I’m good to support the amendment language.

— Rishi
Head of Sales Ops

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@apexanalytics.com>
Cc: Apex Analytics Procurement <procurement@apexanalytics.com>, monica_patel@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-23T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: 9-month price hold + bridge credits (draft)

Hi Elena — thanks for taking the call yesterday. Per our discussion attached is a short-form proposal. Highlights: 

1) 9-month price hold: Redwood will hold current list unit price for incremental +40% capacity through Dec 31, 2027, assuming a signed upsell amendment by April 10, 2027.
2) Bridge credits: $75,000 in one-time credits to apply to incremental overage between May 1 and renewal (non-refundable, expire 2027-12-31).
3) Utilization protection: if incremental capacity utilization <55% for three months in a row, incremental units revert to pay-as-you-go for that tranche.
4) Convert clause: if Apex signs an annual expand commit >150% of current baseline within 60 days after renewal, Redwood will rebate up to 30% of the bridge credits applied (capped at $30k).

Attachment: proposed_amendment_v1.pdf (short-form amendment draft)

Please review and let me know feedback. If this looks close we can push a DocuSign amendment for procurement sign-off.

Best,
Priyom
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@apexanalytics.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Apex Analytics Procurement <procurement@apexanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-03-28T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: 9-month price hold + bridge credits (draft)

Priyom — this looks good and addresses procurement’s main asks. Two quick edits from our side: 1) extend DocuSign signature window to April 17 to accommodate our fiscal review; 2) make the conversion rebate wording explicit that it only applies to credits actually used (not the full $75k pool).

If you can make those two small edits, procurement is ready to move and I’ll route to legal for a final minute review. We’d like to have the pilot capacity active May 1.

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Cloud AI Platforms
Apex Analytics

DocuSign: https://docusign.net/Elena/APX-amendment-0327
